title: 第三章 微光第四章 滴水痕
content_zh:
磨刀的声音持续了将近一个时辰。
当陈默终于停下时，整条手臂都已经麻木得不像是自己的。他松开手，柴刀“哐当”一声掉在青石上，在寂静的夜里格外刺耳。他瘫坐在地上，大口喘着气，汗水顺着下巴滴落，在泥地上洇开一小片深色。
缓了好一会儿，他才重新捡起柴刀，用指尖轻轻触碰刃口。
不一样了。
之前的钝刃摸上去是圆滑的、滞涩的，现在指尖传来的是清晰的、锐利的触感，虽然依旧称不上锋利，但已经能感觉到那种细微的、仿佛要划破皮肤的锋芒。
他又舀来一点水，浇在刀身上，冲掉那些黑色的、混杂着石粉和铁屑的泥浆。昏黄的光线下，刀身映出模糊的、扭曲的倒影，倒影里是一张沾满汗水和尘土的、年轻却过分平静的脸。
陈默看了一会儿，然后收起柴刀和磨刀石，用破布仔细包好，放回铺位下。
做完这一切，他才走到屋檐下那个熟悉的位置，铺开草垫，开始今日的炼气吐纳。
夜风比昨日更冷了些，带着初春深夜特有的、沁入骨髓的寒意。陈默闭上眼睛，调整呼吸，试图捕捉那虚无缥缈的“气感”。
黑暗，沉寂，只有远处夜枭偶尔的啼叫，和风吹过屋瓦的呜呜声。
丹田处空空如也，经脉里也感受不到任何流动的暖意。只有白日劳作留下的酸痛，和此刻寒冷带来的僵硬，真实而顽固地盘踞在身体的每一个角落。
他没有急躁。急躁是无用的。他只是按照《引气诀》所述，一遍又一遍，在呼吸的间隙，在心跳的罅隙里，寻找着。
一炷香过去了。
两炷香过去了。
腿开始发麻，寒意顺着脊椎往上爬。就在他以为今夜又将一无所获时——
一丝极其微弱、微弱到几乎以为是错觉的暖意，突然从丹田深处，极其缓慢地，极其艰难地，向上浮起。
像冬日深潭底，一个即将破碎的气泡。
陈默的呼吸骤然屏住。他不敢动，甚至不敢将注意力完全集中过去，生怕那一点微光般的触感，会因为自己的“注视”而惊散。
他维持着原有的呼吸节奏，只是将意念放得更轻，更柔，如一片羽毛，轻轻拂过那丝暖意经过的路径。
暖意很弱，流动得极慢，像一条将涸的溪流，在干涸的河床上艰难蜿蜒。它沿着《引气诀》上那条最基础的、被称为“气脉”的路径，极其缓慢地向上，经过小腹，经过胸口，然后……停滞了。

前方仿佛有一堵无形的、厚重的墙，将那股微弱的暖流牢牢挡住。
陈默没有强行冲击。他记得《引气诀》上说的：水到渠成，强求反损。他只是耐心地维持着那一点点意念的引导，让暖流在受阻处缓缓盘桓，温养，渗透。
时间一点点流逝。那丝暖流在“墙”前盘旋了许久，终于，像是耗尽了最后一点力气，开始缓缓退却，沿着来路，一点一点，缩回丹田深处，消失不见。
仿佛从未出现过。
陈默缓缓睁开眼睛。
天色依旧漆黑，远处主峰的轮廓在夜色中沉默矗立。他低头，看向自己的双手。手掌粗糙，沾着石粉和铁锈，在昏暗光线下，和两个时辰前没有任何区别。
但他知道，有什么东西不一样了。
那丝暖意，比以往任何一次都要清晰，持续的时间也更长。虽然依旧没能完成一个完整的周天，虽然微弱到几乎可以忽略不计，但它确实出现了。
他静静坐着，感受着身体内部残留的、几乎难以察觉的余温。很微弱，像火柴燃尽后那一星即将熄灭的火光。但那是光。
许久，他才起身，收起草垫。双腿因为久坐而酸麻，他扶着墙，慢慢活动了一下，然后走回通铺。
躺下时，隔壁铺位的王虎在梦里嘟囔了一句什么，翻了个身。鼾声依旧此起彼伏。
陈默闭上眼。他没有立刻入睡，而是在心里，将刚才那丝暖流运行的路径，又细细回想了一遍。从何处起，至何处止，在何处滞涩，在何处回旋。
然后，他将这些记忆，和那张“日课”纸上的每一个字，一起，刻进脑海深处。
寅时三刻，陈默准时醒来。
冷水擦身，站桩。今日的桩功，似乎比昨日更稳了一些。酸痛依旧，寒意依旧，但身体深处，那一点点几乎不存在的暖意余韵，让肌肉的颤抖似乎减弱了分毫。
卯时，他带上磨好的柴刀，再次上山。
今日的柴刀果然不一样了。砍向树干时，不再是那种沉闷的、用死力才能劈进去的感觉，刃口能更轻易地切入木质，省力了不少。他依旧专注，调整着角度和力道，一砍，一撬，树干断裂的声音都比往日清脆了些。
content_en:
The sound of sharpening the knife lasted for nearly an hour.
When Chen Mo finally stopped, his entire arm was too numb to be his own. He let go of his hand, and the hatchet fell on the bluestone with a clang, which was particularly harsh in the silent night. He collapsed on the ground, gasping for air. Sweat dripped down his chin and spread a small patch of dark color on the muddy ground.
After a while, he picked up the hatchet again and gently touched the blade with his fingertips.
It’s different.
The dull blade before felt smooth and dull, but now there is a clear and sharp touch from the fingertips. Although it is still not sharp, you can already feel the subtle edge that seems to cut through the skin.
He scooped up some more water and poured it on the blade to wash away the black mud mixed with stone powder and iron filings. Under the dim light, the blade of the sword reflected a blurry and distorted reflection. In the reflection was a young but overly calm face stained with sweat and dust.
Chen Mo looked at it for a while, then put away the hatchet and whetstone, carefully wrapped them in rags, and put them back under the bunk.
After doing all this, he walked to the familiar position under the eaves, spread out the straw mat, and started today's Qi refining and breathing.
The night wind was a little colder than yesterday, carrying the bone-chilling chill that is unique to late nights in early spring. Chen Mo closed his eyes, adjusted his breathing, and tried to capture the ethereal "aura".
Dark and silent, only the occasional cry of night owls in the distance and the whine of the gentle wind blowing through the roof tiles.
The Dantian was empty, and no flowing warmth could be felt in the meridians. Only the soreness left by the day's work and the stiffness caused by the cold at this moment are truly and stubbornly entrenched in every corner of the body.
He wasn't impatient. Impatience is useless. He just followed the "Qi-Entraining Technique", over and over again, looking for it in the gaps between breaths and heartbeats.
A stick of incense passed.
Two sticks of incense passed.
My legs started to feel numb, and a chill crawled up my spine. Just when he thought he would get nothing again tonight——
An extremely weak warmth, so weak that it was almost thought to be an illusion, suddenly rose up from the depths of the Dantian, extremely slowly and with great difficulty.
Like a bubble about to burst at the bottom of a deep pool in winter.
Chen Mo's breath suddenly stopped. He didn't dare to move, or even fully concentrate on it, for fear that the glimmer of touch would be frightened away by his "gazing".
He maintained the original breathing rhythm, but let his thoughts become lighter and softer, like a feather, gently brushing the path of the warmth.
The warmth was very weak and flowed very slowly, like a dry stream meandering hard on a dry river bed. It followed the most basic path called "qi meridians" in "Qi-Yin Jue", moved upward extremely slowly, passed through the lower abdomen, passed through the chest, and then... stagnated.
There seemed to be an invisible, thick wall in front of him, firmly blocking the weak warm current.
Chen Mo did not attack forcefully. He remembered what was said in "The Art of Entraining Qi": When things come naturally, force will cause damage. He just patiently maintained the guidance of that little bit of thought, allowing the warm current to slowly linger, warm, and penetrate where it was blocked.
Time passes little by little. The warm current hovered in front of the "wall" for a long time, and finally, as if it had exhausted its last bit of strength, it began to retreat slowly, along the path it came from, bit by bit, retracted into the depths of the Dantian and disappeared.
It's like it never happened.
Chen Mo slowly opened his eyes.
The sky was still dark, and the outline of the main peak in the distance stood silently in the night. He lowered his head and looked at his hands. The palm was rough, stained with stone dust and rust. Under the dim light, it looked no different from two hours ago.
But he knew something was different.
The warmth was clearer than ever before and lasted longer. Although it still failed to complete a complete week, although it was so weak that it was almost negligible, it didappeared.
He sat quietly, feeling the almost imperceptible residual warmth remaining inside his body. It's very faint, like the extinguishing light of a match after it burns out. But that's light.
After a long time, he stood up and put away the mat. His legs were numb from sitting for a long time. He supported the wall and slowly moved around, then walked back to the main bunk.
When he lay down, Wang Hu, who was in the next bunk, muttered something in his sleep and turned over. The snoring continued one after another.
Chen Mo closed his eyes. He did not fall asleep immediately, but in his mind, he carefully recalled the path of the warm current just now. Where does it start, where does it end, where does it stagnate, where does it circle.
Then, he engraved these memories into the depths of his mind, along with every word on the "daily lesson" paper.
At three o'clock in the morning, Chen Mo woke up on time.
Wipe your body with cold water and stand still. Today's pile work seems to be more stable than yesterday. The soreness was still there, the chill was still there, but deep in the body, the almost non-existent aftertaste of warmth seemed to weaken the tremors of the muscles.
At nine o'clock, he took the sharpened hatchet and went up the mountain again.
Today's hatchets are indeed different. When chopping at a tree trunk, it no longer has the boring feeling of having to exert all your strength to get in. The blade can cut into the wood more easily, saving a lot of effort. He remained focused, adjusting the angle and strength. With each cut and pry, the sound of the tree trunk breaking was crisper than before.
